sentences.text: The present criminal revision petition has been filed u/s 397 CrPC as to the legality or propriety of the impugned order dated 23.09.2022 passed by Ld. MM08, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi in Complaint Case no. 1065/2021 titled Smt. Savita Pihal v. Nirmal Preet Kaur & ors,

sentences.text:
whereby the Ld.
MM pleased to dismiss the application u/s 156(3) CrPC moved by the revisionist.

2. The impugned order is sought to be assailed on the ground that the impugned order was passed without taking into consideration the facts of the present case and suffers infirmity as Ld. MM has failed to consider the ingredients of the offence alleged by the revisionist by way of her complaint u/s 156(3) CrPC.

It is argued that Ld. MM has not considered that the revisionist is under persistent threat of being killed in the hands of the respondents and hence, further investigation is required into the allegations of the revisionist.
3. I have heard and considered the submissions made by Ld. Counsel for the revisionist and also gone through the material available on record alongwith Trial Court Record.
4. As per the brief facts of the complaint filed by the petitioner before the Ld. MM that Ajay Kumar Pihal, son of revisionist, was married to Nirmal Preet Kaur (hereinafter referred to as 'Respondent no. 1') on 17.01.2019 at Zirakpur, Punjab.
The marriage was solemnized without exchange of dowry and Respondent no. 1 was provided all the freedom in her matrimonial house by the revisionist as her own daughter.

After some time, respondent no. 1 started quarreling with the revisionist and her family members at the instance of her parents, namely, Jaswant Kaur and Ram Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'Respondent no. 2' and 'Respondent no. 3') and her brother Surinder Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'Respondent no. 4').
Such instigations on the part of Respondent no. 2 to 4 created lot of disturbance in the house of the revisionist.

During stay of Respondent no. 1 at her inlaws house, she used to visit her parents home at Punjab many times without taking care of her own family needs and whenever, the revisionist objected to her said behaviour, she always threatened to lodge a false case against her under the vanity of her contacts with higher ups in Punjab and Haryana.
It is alleged that on 12.02.2019, Respondent no. 1 mis behaved with the revisionist by using filthy language.
On 26.03.2019, her parents (Respondent no. 2 and 3) instigated Respondent no. 1 to fight with the revisionist.
On 28.05.2019, a quarrel had taken place in which Respondent no. 1 allegedly misbehaved with the revisionist.
It is also alleged that she was having several male friends and she was even noticed while being in intimate talks with them by the neighbours.
It is further alleged that on 28.05.2019, Respondent no. 1 left her matrimonial home with all her precious jewellery and articles to live in Punjab with her parents.

It is also alleged that on the instigation of Respondent no. 2 to Respondent no. 4, Respondent no. 1 created ugly scenes in the house of the revisionist and put the revisionist under the persistent intimidation of committing suicide by her.

It is also alleged that Respondent no. 1 gave birth to a male child but her son and the revisionist Savita Pihal vs Nirmal Preet Kaur on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78346085/
2 were not allowed to meet the child.

sentences.text: It is also alleged that on 11.07.2019 under the aid and advice of her parents (Respondent no. 2 and 3), Respondent no. 1 lodged a false complaint against the revisionist u/s 498A IPC and u/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
It is also alleged that on 11.08.2019, respondent no. 2 and 4 forcibly entered the house of the revisionist, misbehaved with her and threatened her and also used filthy language.
5. Ld. Trial Court has also called Action Taken Report from the concerned Police Station and also considered the same while passing the impugned order.
As per the status report, it is revealed that from the enquiry conducted so far, the present matter is a matrimonial/family dispute.

6. As revisionist has herself submitted that a case has already been registered against the revisionist u/s 498A IPC and the present complaint also states about the filing of the said FIR by Respondent no. 1 against the revisionist and her son.

The said FIR has been registered on 30.11.2021 in which Respondent no. 1 has alleged against her inlaws including the revisionist about the demand of dowry and cruelty on account of the same and the said matter is stated to be still pending.

The allegations which have been raised by way of present complaint are in the category of family dispute in which the revisionist herself has specifically narrated all the incidents in which she felt aggrieved by the act and conduct of Respondent no. 1.
The present complaint deals with several small incidents of quarrel and household disputes.
There has been some instances of misbehaviour and quarrel which are brought on record by the revisionist.

7. On perusal of the contents of the complaint as well as the documents placed alongwith the complaint, I am of the view that revisionist herself is in possession of all the evidence on the basis of which she wants to proceed against the respondents for a criminal action and for collection of the same, intervention of police is not required.
The present complaint is even not spared from the doubt from being a counter blast to the complaint lodged by Respondent no. 1 against the revisionist.
The averments made in the present complaint by Respondent no. 1 could be the defence of the revisionist against the respondents in the said case registered on the complaint of Respondent no. 1.
The power to direct investigation u/s 156 (3) Cr.PC is to be read with section 190 Cr.PC.

When the complaint is filed before the Magistrate, he do have two options, one is to proceed u/s 156 (3)
Cr.PC and direct the registration of FIR and other option is to proceed u/s 200 Cr.PC for recording of the evidence of the complainant.

8. It has been held by Hon'ble High Court while laying down several guidelines in Subh Karan Luharuka vs. State (170) 2010 DLT 516 that : "However, in that case the Magistrate, before passing any order to proceed under chapter XII, should not only satisfied himself about the pre requisites as aforesaid, but, additionally, he should also be satisfied that it is necessary to direct the police investigation in the matter for conclusion of evidence which is neither in the possession of the complainant nor can be produced by the witness on being summoned by the court at the instance of complainant, and the matter is as such which calls for investigation by the state agency.

entities.text: Subh Karan Luharuka vs. State (170) 2010 DLT 516
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The magistrate must pass an order giving cogent reasons as to why he intend to proceed under Chapter XII instead of Chapter XV of the code".

sentences.text: "Thus the Magistrate is not supposed to act mechanically and direct the registration of FIR in each and every case in routine and casual manner.
Criminal law is not expected to be set in motion on mere asking of a party.

There has to be some substance in the complaint file and it is only if it appears that the allegations are serious enough and establish the commission of cognizable offence required through investigation by the police, an FIR should be ordered to be registered."

9. As a cumulative effect of the above discussion, I do not find any infirmity in the order of the Ld.
Trial Court.
Therefore, the present revision petition stands dismissed.
10. Trial Court Record be sent back with the copy of this order.
11. File of criminal revision be consigned to record room.
